newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Three Papua New Guinea men sentenced to hang.
newsitem.headline: Three Papua New Guinea men sentenced to hang.

text.p: A Papua New Guinea court on Monday sentenced three men to hang for the murder of a woman in a village in 1995, according to media in the South Pacific nation.
If the sentences are carried out the men will be the first executed since the South Pacific nation reintroduced the death penalty for wilful murder in 1991.

The Kimbe National Court on New Britain island sentenced Steven Loke, Greg Kavoa and Charles Kaona to death for the so-called pay back murder of Agnes Banovo on December 3, 1995, said Frank Kolma, editor of The National newspaper in the capital Port Moresby.
Pay back murder is when a person kills for revenge and is common in Papua New Guinea.

The three men abducted Banovo from her village after she was unable to tell them the whereabouts of her son, who the men believed had killed one of their villagers, the Australian Broadcasting Corporation radio reported from Port Moresby.

The men dragged Banovo by her lap-lap (skirt), which was tied around her neck, to their nearby village of Pangalu, raped her and then used knives to chop at her head and neck until she died. Banovo's skull was smashed, her spine fractured, and she was stabbed in the chest and neck. Judge Robert Woods said among the state's witnesses was the woman's 10-year-old son, who identified one of the three men and said his mother told him to go home as she was going to die.
Other witnesses told of hearing Agnes cry out to her attackers to kill her properly and not just keep cutting at her, said an ABC reporter.
Sentencing the three to hang, Woods said pay back murder of an innocent victim was in the worst category of homicide.
The three may still appeal the ruling.
The only other person sentenced to hang under the reintroduced death penalty won an appeal. The last hanging was in 1957.
